1.explanation:
• withGetArgs (in src/ol/expr/expression.js) is the argument validator that recognizes the ‘get’ operator and records which feature properties will be accessed. It never treats ‘id’ as a special case, so feature.getId() is never added to the parsing context.  
• parseCallExpression (in src/ol/expr/expression.js) invokes the parser created for each operator, including ‘get’; since no parser handles a standalone ‘id’ operator, calls to fetch id fall through.  
• Operators (in src/ol/style/expressions.js) is the registry of style‐expression operators (including ‘get’). It has no entry for ‘id’, and the existing ‘get’ implementation only works against properties.  
• expressionToGlsl (in src/ol/style/expressions.js) turns parsed expressions into GLSL code. Its logic for the ‘get’ operator generates code invoking feature.get('attr') and cannot generate feature.getId().

To support reading id, the parser must either extend the existing ‘get’ handler (withGetArgs) to detect when the attribute name is ‘id’ and register a callback against feature.getId(), or add a new ‘id’ operator (in Operators and in expressionToGlsl) that emits the correct call. parseCallExpression must be updated to route that operator name to the new handler as well.
1.bug_scenario: When writing a style expression against a GeoJSON source, users expect to be able to fetch a feature’s “id” (i.e. what you get from feature.getId()) via the same bracketed operators used for properties (`['get', '…']`). Currently the expression parser only looks in the feature’s properties collection, so passing `['get','id']` does nothing (or errors) and there is no standalone `['id']` operator. In short, style expressions can read properties but not the feature id.

2.explanation:
All of the listed elements participate in parsing, compiling and code‐generation for the ‘get’ operator:  

• CallExpression is the AST node created for any operator call, including ['get', …].  It underlies how ‘get’ expressions are represented.  
• withGetArgs in src/ol/expr/expression.js validates and pulls the attribute name from the encoded array and records it in the parsing context.properties; it needs to be extended to recognize 'id' and not just properties in feature.properties.  
• parseCallExpression dispatches on the operator name ('get') and builds a CallExpression via createParser/withGetArgs; it will need a special branch for 'id' or allow 'get' to accept 'id' (and possibly ignore the type hint).  
• compileAccessorExpression in src/ol/expr/cpu.js turns a CallExpression with operator 'get' into an evaluator function (e.g. ctx.properties[name] or feature.get(name)).  It needs to be updated so that when name==='id' it calls feature.getId() instead of reading from ctx.properties.  
• expressionToGlsl in src/ol/style/expressions.js emits GLSL code for style expressions.  For ['get','attr'] it injects code to fetch a vertex attribute or uniform; it must be updated to generate the correct shader code for retrieving a feature’s id (possibly via a varying or a special built‐in).  

Together these cover all stages—parsing the expression, representing it, evaluating it on the CPU, and compiling it to GLSL on the GPU—so they are the key places to modify to support reading feature.id.
2.bug_scenario: Currently MapLibre’s style‐expression system lets you fetch any feature property via ["get","attributeName"] (which is mapped to feature.get('attributeName')), but there’s no way to read a feature’s id through an expression.  In GeoJSON the id lives at the root level, not in properties, so expressions like ["get","id"] simply fail and force users to duplicate id into properties.  The user wants ["get","id"] (or a dedicated ["id"] operator) to map to feature.getId() so they can style by feature id without duplicating it.
